lines: An eight by eight grid of stereo loops, one track per column, that records and launches takes on the beats of a NINJAM jam clock
Note — Placed immediately beside a Ninjam module, on either side, it takes that room's tempo and interval; standing alone it runs on a simulated interval whose length is set in the menu
Note — A press does not act at once: it is queued, shown by a blinking outline, and commits on the next beat. One queued press per track, and the last press wins
Note — A launched take cycles at the length and speed it was recorded at, so a tempo change on the server leaves it running as it was; only queued presses and a recording in flight are cancelled
Note — A recording caps at one interval. Carry on playing and the take chains into the next empty cell down the column until an interval comes in quiet; the chain then replays from its first cell
Note — Click a track's name strip to rename it, up to four characters. With a MindMeld MixMaster feeding INS the names copy between the two on their own
Note — Every committed take is written as an OGG file under the jam folder, and the grid comes back with the patch
Note — Nothing reaches a NINJAM room by itself: patch MIX into a Ninjam module's input jacks to transmit the submix
Press it empty to start recording on the next beat, filled to launch it, playing to stop it; press it while recording to close the take on the next beat and loop it, or press again to keep recording
Launches every filled cell in its row and stops the track under every empty one, on the next beat; the last scene pressed wins
Stops whatever that track is playing, and throws away a recording in progress on it
Stops every track, and throws away any recording in progress
Puts that track's incoming audio on air, green feeding it into MIX for the room, cyan keeping it private by routing it to CUE instead
Latches overdub on, so the selected playing cell keeps layering what comes in each time round until it is switched off
The left channel of that track's own input; patching it makes the track take its audio from its own pair of jacks rather than from INS
The right channel of that track's own input; with nothing patched, the track's left jack feeds both sides
Feeds all eight tracks down one poly cable, channels 1 and 2 going to track 1, channels 3 and 4 to track 2 and so on; a track whose own left jack is patched takes that instead of its pair here
Carries the eight tracks down one poly cable, channels 1 and 2 for track 1, channels 3 and 4 for track 2 and so on
The left side of the private monitor mix, carrying the tracks whose transmit latch is off
The right side of the private monitor mix, carrying the tracks whose transmit latch is off
The left side of the submix of the tracks that are on air; patch it to a Ninjam module's left input to transmit it
The right side of the submix of the tracks that are on air; patch it to a Ninjam module's right input to transmit it
Menu — Simulated interval (when no Ninjam clock) — sets the interval the grid runs at when no Ninjam module is beside it, from 2 seconds up to 32 seconds
Menu — New clips: repeats — sets how many times a newly recorded take plays before it stops, the infinity choice leaving it cycling
Menu — New clips: decay per repetition — sets how far a newly recorded take drops in level each time round, down to -6dB
Menu — Capture: auto-advance while playing — when off, a recording that runs past the end of the interval stops there instead of chaining into the next empty cell down the column
Menu — Clear all slots — empties every cell in the grid
Menu — Choose folder… — picks the folder the recorded takes are written to
Menu — Reset to ~/Music/jams — puts the take folder back to the default
Menu — Open this session's folder — opens the folder holding this session's takes
Menu — New session (keep loops) — starts a fresh session folder and leaves the takes in the grid
Menu — New session (clear grid) — starts a fresh session folder and empties the grid
Menu — Embed takes in patch — when on, the recorded audio is stored inside the patch file, so a shared patch carries its loops with it
Menu — Repeats — on a grid cell's own right-click menu: how many times that take plays before it stops
Menu — Decay per repetition — on a grid cell's own right-click menu: how far that take drops in level each time round
Menu — After — on a grid cell's own right-click menu: whether that take stops when it is done, or launches a numbered slot in the same track
Menu — Clear slot — on a grid cell's own right-click menu: empties that cell
Menu — Reset to default — on a track name's own right-click menu: puts that track's name back to its default

Looper.notes: The track name strips, the waveform displays and the grid's blinking queue outlines are drawn inside custom widgets rather than as ParamWidgets, so clicking them cannot reach this help; the rename gesture is recorded in a Note line instead. lines: A client for NINJAM online jam rooms: it plays a room's public stream, or joins the room's protocol to decode every player's audio and upload your own
Note — Picking a room and listening plays its public stream and sends nothing. Joining the protocol puts the input jacks on the air, and a reloaded patch rejoins without transmitting until you say so
Note — The Looper belongs immediately to the left and the Recorder immediately to the right; both work only while they touch this module, and the menu will place either one
Note — The server login and the display name are kept in a private file in the Rack user folder rather than in the patch, so a shared patch carries neither
Note — The clock, reset, run and phase jacks stay at 0V until the room reports a tempo and an interval length
Mixes the metronome click into the MAIN outputs; the click jack carries the tone whether this is on or off
Your audio into the room, one poly channel per NINJAM channel you have declared; it is uploaded only while you are joined and transmitting
The right side of your audio into the room, one poly channel per NINJAM channel; with nothing patched, the left jack feeds both sides
The left side of the room's mix, summed from every player when joined or taken from the public stream when listening, with the metronome folded in while its toggle is on
The right side of the room's mix, summed from every player when joined or taken from the public stream when listening, with the metronome folded in while its toggle is on
The left side of each player's own audio, one poly channel per player in the room; it carries nothing while a public stream is playing rather than the room being joined
The right side of each player's own audio, one poly channel per player in the room; it carries nothing while a public stream is playing rather than the room being joined
The metronome tone, a sine burst decaying over about 35ms on every beat, pitched at 1760Hz on the interval's first beat and 880Hz on the rest
A 10V gate with equal time high and low, pulsing the number of times per beat chosen in the menu
A 10V pulse over the first half of the interval's first beat
10V while the room's tempo and interval are known and the clock is running, and 0V otherwise
A ramp from 0V to 10V across one interval, dropping back to 0V at the downbeat
Menu — Display name (public jams) — the name shown to the other players in the room
Menu — Refresh room list — fetches the directory of public rooms again
Menu — Stop — leaves the room, or stops the public stream being listened to
Menu — Add Looper (left) — places a Looper module immediately to the left
Menu — Add Recorder (right) — places a Recorder module immediately to the right
Menu — Metronome click — mixes the click tone into the MAIN outputs
Menu — MIDI metronome: toggle on trigger (notes/pads) — when on, a mapped MIDI control flips the metronome on each rising edge, rather than its value being read as the on or off state
Menu — Clock: pulses per beat — sets how many pulses the clock jack sends in each beat, chosen from 1, 2, 4, 8 and 24
Menu — Low (~135 kbps) — encodes your transmitted audio at the lowest of the three qualities offered
Menu — Medium (~190 kbps) — encodes your transmitted audio at the middle of the three qualities offered
Menu — High (~235 kbps) — encodes your transmitted audio at the highest of the three qualities offered

Menu — Voice mode (live, unsynced) — sends your audio as NINJAM voice chat: capture starts the moment you transmit and the other players hear it as it arrives, rather than aligned to the interval grid

Ninjam.notes: The room browser, the chat console, the peak meter and the transmit lamp are custom widgets rather than ParamWidgets, so no click on them reaches this help; what a reader needs from them is in the Note lines. The 1760Hz and 880Hz click pitches, the 35ms decay and the pulse widths are all in src/Ninjam.cpp around lines 915-960. The metronome switch and the menu item named Metronome click are the same setting.

lines: Archives a NINJAM jam to disk as each player's raw OGG intervals with an index beside them, and exports the result as a session file for Ableton
Note — It records nothing unless it is placed immediately beside a Ninjam module; on its own it can only export a jam folder recorded earlier
Note — Recordings go into a dated folder under the jams folder, with a JSON lines index placing every interval on the session timeline
Note — The audio is stored as the bytes that came off the wire, with no re-encoding
Note — Nothing is written unless this module is armed next to a joined Ninjam module
Arms the archive, so every interval the room sends is written to disk from the moment it is switched on
Includes your own transmitted mix in the archive alongside the other players'
Menu — Export Ableton Live set (.als)… — prompts for a jam folder and writes a session file from its recordings: the Looper grid as clips, each player on an arrangement lane, tempo and bars matching
Menu — Export .als when recording stops — when on, the session file is built automatically as soon as recording ends
Menu — Target Live edition: Standard / Suite (full), Lite (8 tracks: 6 loops + players + TX) — chooses a track per player, or a fold-down to eight tracks with every player merged onto one lane
Menu — Choose folder… — picks the folder the jam recordings are written to
Menu — Reset to ~/Music/jams — puts the jams folder back to the default
Menu — Open jams folder — opens the jams folder in the file browser
Recorder.notes: The interval counter display is a custom widget, not a ParamWidget. The export menu items work whether or not a Ninjam module is adjacent; the folder items appear only when one is, because the rest of the menu returns early without a link (src/Recorder.cpp:347-350).

lines: Plays an internet radio stream, Icecast or plain HTTP, into a patch through a level control
Note — Click the station picture to open the picker and choose a station, or step through the whole list with the arrows; the choice is saved with the patch and reconnects when it is loaded
Note — The lamp lights only while audio is really decoding, not merely because the server answered. When a connection fails, the reason is printed where the artwork goes
Note — To add a station of your own, right-click, paste a stream or playlist address into the field under the stream URL label, and press Enter
Note — A pasted address is checked in the background: the module confirms audio really flows, fetches a name and icon from radio-browser, and saves it. An unrecognised stream plays, then you name it
Note — MP3, AAC and HLS streams play on every platform
Note — The bundled stations are ordinary Rack presets, so they also appear under the Preset menu
Sets the output level, silent at the bottom and +12dB at the top, the gain following the square of the knob position as the VCV AUDIO module's does
Starts and stops the stream
Scales the level set by the knob: 0V silences the output and 10V leaves the knob's level alone, with anything outside that range clamped to it
The left channel of the stream, at line level after the level control
The right channel of the stream, at line level after the level control
Menu — Play — connects to the current station and starts it; the same item reads Stop while a stream is playing
Menu — MIDI play: toggle on trigger (notes/pads) — when on, a mapped MIDI control flips play on each rising edge, rather than its value being read as the play state

Radio.notes: The station picture, the up and down steppers and the status text are custom widgets with no ParamWidget, so they cannot be clicked for help; they are covered by Note lines. The level knob's +12dB top comes from configParam's dB display (src/Radio.cpp:155, displayBase -10, multiplier 40) and from the panel lettering drawn at src/Radio.cpp:54-55. The CV input multiplies the knob rather than adding to it, so there is no sum to clamp.
